focus_relevance_note: Live piano-trio-plays-popular-material blueprint — Garner's million-selling 1955 Carmel concert is the commercial proof Lewis's 1965 formula starts from.
Chicago Argo precedent — Cuban-derived standard read through Jamal's space-and-dynamics piano trio language, the foundational model Lewis names in interviews as his template.
Same-era black-pianist soul-jazz crossover via modal ostinato on Blue Note — opposite-coast parallel proving the In Crowd moment is the ensemble-wide gesture, not a Lewis solo invention.

Transatlantic parallel — Burdon/Price's Hammond-Vox arrangement reverse-distills a public-domain folk source into UK R&B authorship one year before Lewis does the same with Dobie Gray on the Argo side.
Source song. Billy Page wrote it; Gray turned it into a mod-anthem on Charger 105 Oct 1964 — the R&B vocal object Lewis will reverse-distill seven months later.

Anchor. Bohemian Caverns clap-along makes the audience the rhythm section; Lewis strips Gray's lyric and reverse-distills R&B vocal authorship into a soul-jazz piano-trio statement, Billboard #5 / Grammy 1965.

Closes the triple-translation triptych — John Phillips re-translates Lewis's instrumental groove back into four-part folk-rock vocal harmony on the Feb 1966 debut LP. Fourteen months Gray-to-Mamas end-to-end.

UK Mod mirror — Soho Flamingo Club resident reverse-distills Mongo Santamaría's Latin-jazz tune via Lambert-Hendricks-Ross vocalese into a UK #1 Jan 1965, the parallel transatlantic invention of the same gesture months before Lewis.
Same-year sequel — Lewis reverse-distills The McCoys' rock #1 four months after the anchor (Billboard #11 Dec 1965), proving the cover-as-authorship template is a working practice, not a one-off.

Formula extended across sacred/secular — Lewis distills a traditional African-American spiritual with the new trio (Maurice White drums, Cleveland Eaton bass), Billboard #19, gold cert. Source category leap from pop/rock to gospel.

Methodological descent — Capitol Studio A audience hand-picked into the room; Zawinul's gospel-soul vamp engineered for 'live' atmosphere as the studio-side answer to Lewis's actual Bohemian Caverns night. Billboard #11.
Personnel diaspora — Eldee Young and Red Holt, Lewis's In Crowd rhythm section, continue the soul-jazz singles gesture under their own name on Brunswick (#3 Hot 100, #1 Cash Box, gold).

artist: Julie Driscoll, Brian Auger & The Trinity
focus_relevance_note: UK Hammond-soul-jazz translation of a 1967 Dylan/Danko basement obscurity — Driscoll's voice + Auger's organ vamp turn folk-rock into UK #5 dancefloor authorship inside the mod-aftermath Hammond scene Lewis was canon for.
Late evolution — Lewis with ex-drummer Maurice White's Earth, Wind & Fire; the cover-as-authorship gesture migrates into peer co-authorship of jazz-funk-disco hybrid, his biggest 70s seller.

Foundational UK Acid Jazz Hammond revival — Lalo Schifrin's TV theme read as soul-jazz dancefloor instrumental on Re-Elect The President 1986, the scene built explicitly on rediscovered Cadet/Blue Note 60s singles (Lewis prominently).

Acid Jazz label flagship — late-80s UK musicians reverse-engineer early-70s American soul-jazz (Lewis, Crusaders, Ayers) into contemporary club-soul, the scene's origin in mod-revival Lewis spins made literal.

First Blue Note platinum LP — Wilkinson licenses Hancock's 1964 Cantaloupe Island whole and raps over it. Sample-as-authorship matures the In Crowd cover-as-authorship gesture into the 90s, closing the arc.
Acid Jazz Records origin reaching commercial peak — clavinet/horns/falsetto setup re-encodes the 1965 'small combo with insistent groove → pop charts' instinct three decades downstream (UK #10).
